subject: Dedicated lanes: token & throughput slab qualification and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@corvushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + numbers we discussed (token volumes, budget window, GPU preference)

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and items we agreed to validate so we can size a Dedicated lane proposal: 

Key customer context (from call)
- Primary workload: conversational customer support + short-document augmentation (avg response length ~420 tokens)
- Typical using pattern: steady weekday traffic with 7M tokens/day avg, ~20M tokens/day peak during promos
- Latency target: p95 < 450ms for 512-token responses (user-facing)

Budget & unit targets you mentioned
- Internal budget window: $30k–$45k/month (currently being reviewed by procurement)
- Corvus target unit economics: ~$4.50 / 1M tokens as a target to consider commit

Dedicated sizing preferences
- Preferred GPU: H100 if we can keep within budget; A100 acceptable as fall-back for burst lanes
- Desired reserved footprint: looking for a baseline that can cover steady load and allow ~2–3x burst headroom for peak days
- Throughput ask: need to support approx 250 concurrent requests with our average tokens (estimation we used on call) — we flagged this as ~25–40k tokens/sec sustained across the fleet during peak bursts (we'll refine with metrics)

Next steps I promised
- Send an initial pricing sketch + SOW draft for a 12-month reserved lane (baseline + burst) — attachment: Redwood_Corvus_pricing_20270530.xlsx and draft SOW
- Include a throughput mapping showing H100 vs A100 lanes and recommended reserved sizes
- Procurement contact (cc’d in your reply) to confirm contract cadence and PO process

Would you confirm the procurement contact + whether a 12-month term is acceptable? If anything above is off relative to your internal numbers, flag it and we’ll re-run the sizing.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Corvus_pricing_20270530.xlsx, Redwood_draft_SOW_Corvus_20270530.pdf

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@corvushealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@corvushealth.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + numbers we discussed (token volumes, budget window, GPU preference)

Hi Naomi — thanks for the quick recap and the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Numbers look right to first order. Our analytics team will provide a short export tomorrow to validate the 7M / 20M numbers (I asked them to include hourly slices and avg tokens per response).
- Procurement is the right place to loop in: procurement@corvushealth.com (cc’d). They prefer line-item pricing per month and an explicit overage rate if we go above reserved tokens.
- Term: 12 months is our preferred initial term (we can discuss pilot-specific exit language).
- GPU preference: we’d like to anchor on H100 lanes if you can show a cost/throughput map that keeps us near our target $/1M tokens. If the H100 price stretches us past the top of the budget range, we’d consider an H100 baseline with A100 burst lanes.

Procurement asked for: pricing spreadsheet, SOW, and a sample billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) — happy to review once you send.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Platform Engineering | Corvus Health
sam.jenkins@corvushealth.com | +1 (617) 999-0412

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: quick economics + lane mapping for Corvus (H100 vs A100)

Quick internal note (keeping this thread so we preserve context):

Summary of the ask
- Baseline to cover 7M tokens/day steady, headroom to 20M/day peak; latency p95 < 450ms target at avg 512 tokens
- Customer target unit price ~ $4.50 / 1M tokens — procurement will push but that’s the anchor

Proposal sketch (initial thinking)
- Option A (H100 baseline): 2x reserved H100 lanes -> covers steady + modest burst with autoscaling; keep 1x A100 reserved for cheap burst overflow
  - Rough performance anchor: H100 throughput ~3.0x A100 for this model family at 512 tokens (our bench data attached: throughput-bench-H100-A100.csv)
  - Ballpark unit econ (monthly amortized + infra): $5.95 / 1M tokens for H100 baseline at 2x reserved H100 (12mo term, committed tokens calc)

- Option B (A100 baseline + H100 burst): 4x reserved A100 baseline + 1x H100 burst lane
  - Lower committed monthly cost but higher tail latency on heavy bursts; ballpark unit econ: $4.20 / 1M tokens (but may not meet p95 latency target under peaks)

- Other levers: quantization/longer batching windows for night windows (low-risk) to push unit cost down 8–12% without changing hardware commitment

Ask for pricing sheet: Naomi, if you can attach the initial workbook (per Sam request) with the two option tabs we can send the external note; include explicit overage rates (per-1M token) and monthly billing cadence (they asked to compare monthly vs quarterly).

Karthik
VP, Dedicated Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@corvushealth.com>, procurement@corvushealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated lanes: token & throughput slab qualification and next steps

Hi Sam / Corvus procurement — attaching the items we discussed. Summary and ask below.

What we’re sending (attachments)
- Redwood_Corvus_pricing_20270530.xlsx (two tabs: H100-baseline and A100-baseline; includes line-item monthly pricing, committed token buckets, and overage rates)
- Redwood_draft_SOW_Corvus_20270530.pdf (SOW draft for a 12-month committed lane; pilot acceptance criteria and SLA language included)
- throughput-bench-H100-A100.csv (internal bench numbers for the model family used in sizing)

Executive summary (short)
- For your target latency and the 7M / 20M token profile we recommend Option A (H100 baseline): 2x H100 reserved + 1x A100 reserved for cold/burst fallback.
- Ballpark committed unit econ (12mo): ~$5.95 / 1M tokens (H100 baseline). This is above your $4.50 target but preserves p95 latency SLO.
- If hitting the $/1M target is a hard constraint, Option B (A100 baseline + H100 burst) reduces the committed unit cost to ~ $4.20 / 1M but may require a higher burst reserve or acceptance of increased p95 latency during peak days.

Requested next steps
1) Procurement: confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and PO timeline so we can finalize SOW/payment terms.
2) Product/Engineering: once procurement confirms cadence, we’ll schedule a short benching window (48–72 hours) to capture Corvus traffic profile and refine the committed tokens to ensure econ alignment.
3) Go/No-go for a 12mo commit: if Corvus can stretch to $30–45k/month, we’ll finalize Option A pricing; if not, we’ll present a tightened Option B with clear latency trade-offs documented in the SOW.

Please reply with procurement POC and any adjustments to the tokens/day numbers and target unit economics. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: Redwood_Corvus_pricing_20270530.xlsx, Redwood_draft_SOW_Corvus_20270530.pdf, throughput-bench-H100-A100.csv
